core_obligations: Get the constant c_2 from finite length of M/M' and set c_1 equal to that length (proof lines 14273-14274).

For the upper bound, split the length of M/I^{n+1}M into c_1 plus the length of M'/I^{n+1}M, which is at most the corresponding quantity with I^{n+1}M' and hence equals c_1 plus the Hilbert-Samuel value for M' at n (proof lines 14275-14286).
For the lower bound, use I^n M contained in I^{n-c_2}M' for n at least c_2 to compare the lengths in the other direction and obtain c_1 plus the value for M' at n minus c_2 (proof lines 14287-14300).
proof_roadmap: Bound the discrepancy between the two Hilbert-Samuel functions by the length of the quotient (proof lines 14272-14286).
Push the index back by c_2 for the reverse inequality (proof lines 14287-14302).
difficulty_reason: For finite modules M' contained in M with finite length quotient, the lemma produces constants c_1 and c_2 such that the Hilbert-Samuel function of M at n is squeezed between c_1 plus that of M' at n minus c_2 and c_1 plus that of M' at n (statement lines 14261-14270). The proof does not estimate the two functions by polynomials: it takes c_1 to be the length of the quotient, splits the length of M modulo a power of I additively, compares the resulting terms by the containments available inside M', and uses I^{c_2}M contained in M' to shift the index for the other inequality (proof lines 14272-14302). The choice of c_2 and the index shift are the content, and both displayed chains of equalities are given. H2.
